newsitem.title: ISRAEL: Israeli shekel down again against dollar, basket.
newsitem.headline: Israeli shekel down again against dollar, basket.

text.p: The Israeli shekel declined for the fourth consecutive session on Wednesday against the dollar and the basket of foreign currencies in quiet trading, dealers said.
"After three wild days, trading was relatively quiet today and activity was low. Despite that, the shekel continued to decline," said a dealer at Israel Discount Bank.

The shekel fell by almost three percent since Friday after the central bank lowered its key lending rate 1.2 percentage points and the cabinet approved an exchange rate reform which widened the upper limit of the shekel's diagonal trading band. This increased the risk of a depreciation of the shekel, which had been trading at the bottom limit for much of the past year.

"I think that the main reason for shekel's decline is that there are no (dollar) sellers in the market. Last week investors sold many dollars on expectations of the shekel's appreciation (amid rumours that both the upper and lower limit of the band would be widened). Now there are only buyers in the market," the dealer said.
He said that the market was very sensitive and investors nervous. "Despite that I do not think this is a new trend but we still need to see where the market is going."

The representative rate for the dollar was fixed at 3.5240 shekels against 3.5060 on Tuesday. The basket, composed of the dollar, mark, pound sterling, French franc and yen, was fixed at 3.8355 against 3.8142 on Tuesday.
On the crosses, the shekel traded against the yen at 3.0933 shekels per 100 yen compared with 3.0580 on Tuesday, and against the mark at 2.0459 shekels compared with 2.0326 on Tuesday.
After the setting of the representative rate the shekel continued to decline and in late afternoon, the dollar was trading at 3.5480 shekels.
- Dan Gerstenfeld, Tel Aviv newsroom, 972-3-537-2211 x233
